answer.rationale: The release went out 2 hours ago and is the most plausible proximate cause of the 5x p99 latency spike on the write path. memory_b1 documents a prior case where rolling back a release cleared a checkout-error spike and finished without customer impact, which supports rollback as the highest-leverage single intervention available. memory_b4 confirms that circuit breakers contained a dependency outage and preserved the rest of the checkout path, so I want to keep them armed in case the rollback alone does not fully resolve the latency. Settlement writes are at their daily peak and are heavy, which raises the cost of getting the call wrong — but the inherited record is consistent that rollback is reversible and has historically restored stability cleanly. Regional failover and add_capacity are slower and riskier to execute as a single intervention during peak writes. Routing read replicas is irrelevant to a write-path latency regression. A circuit breaker alone would protect against the regression but would not restore write throughput, so it is a complement, not a substitute. I will not pull additional memories because the verification budget is capped at 2 and these two are sufficient to commit. If the rollback does not bring p99 latency back inside the target window in the next 30 minutes, the queued next-step is enable_circuit_breaker to preserve the write path while investigating further.
